findings.text: `Servex/agents/doc/external.md` was not updated even though `External.js` nearly tripled in size (cursor-per-conversation, digest, follows-read-at-`updates`-time, rotation) — it still describes a single `.cursor` file and lists "Files" as only `External.js`/`External.test.mjs`/the two one-liners in `Agents.js`/`Servex.js`, with no mention of `mark-strip.js`, `cursors_file`, `followed_lines`, or `rotate`. `agents/readme.md`'s own Design list points here as the pointer doc for `External.js`, so a fresh agent following that link gets a stale picture; `Servex/ext/remote/doc/catch-up.md` (which this task did update) is the only accurate account.

`Servex/agents/map.md` (the file-by-file index) has no row for the new `Servex/agents/mark-strip.js` — rule "index everything you create" (agents.md law 10); the row for `External.js` there is also now a stale one-liner.

`External.followed_lines(id, state, budget)` is never called when the inbox alone already fills `cap` (budget = 0 short-circuits before checking any follow). `more` can then read `false` even though a followed file has unread lines — no data is lost (the per-file offset isn't touched), but the "N new updates" hint can under-report for one call until the next `updates()` catches up. Not covered by the new tests, which only exercise the followed-budget path against an empty inbox (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, "fix A" block).

`Agents.js`'s new dedup map (`this._done_seen`, `wake_parent` around line 1075) is keyed per `parent:child` and never pruned as children finish; on a long-lived Servex process with many short minions this grows without bound (small strings, but unbounded). findings.text: requirements.md's Tests section names "a followed file truncated" as one of the scenarios the deliverable must prove, and `External.followed_lines` has a dedicated branch for it (`Servex/agents/External.js:200`, `if (size < prev){ state.follows[rel] = size; continue; }`), but no test in `RemoteMCP.test.mjs` or `External.test.mjs` ever shrinks a followed file after it's been read — grepping both files for "truncat" finds nothing. The branch could silently regress (e.g. resend old bytes instead of resetting) and nothing would catch it.

The half-written-last-line case is proven for the inbox file (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, `'{"text":"half'` around the "an unfinished line waits" assertion) but not for a followed file going through `followed_lines` — the loop there (`External.js` around the `nl === -1` break) shares the same idea but is a separate code path and has no equivalent test.
